jobs.title: Treasury Associate
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA; New York, NY; Sandy, UT
jobs.description:
The Company You’ll Join

Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. Built to replace fragmented tools with a single system of record, Carta brings together the software, services, and legal infrastructure that founders use to manage equity, fund managers use to run administration and reporting, and legal teams use to close transactions. Trusted by 55,000 companies and 1.8M+ equity holders in 160+ countries, and 10,000 funds and SPVs representing $250B+ in assets under management, Carta is transforming how private capital operates. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Fast Company, Inc. and Great Places to Work.

For more information about our offices and culture, check out our Carta careers page .

The Problems You'll Solve

At Carta, our employees set out on a mission to unlock the power of equity ownership for more people in more places. We believe that the problems we solve today unlock the opportunities of tomorrow. As a Treasury Associate, you’ll work to:

- Daily Payment Exceptions & Platform Operations: Support payment exceptions handling of transaction failures and provide timely support to cross-functional business and support teams to resolve payment and funding issues in real-time.

- High-Volume Payment Approval & Specialized Disbursements: Oversee the review and approval of daily outgoing payment batches and manage the end-to-end disbursement and daily reconciliation processes for specialized corporate or transactional bank accounts.

- Bank Portal Security & Compliance Controls: Mitigate platform and transaction risks by administering daily fraud controls and reviewing transaction exception items across primary banking portals, while coordinating timely responses to banking compliance and regulatory inquiries.

- Daily Bank Data & Limit Monitoring: Maintain master banking data records and perform daily tracking and analysis of credit limits to support credit risk management and underwriting activities.

- Monthly Banking Audits & Statement Administration: Own monthly bank statement collection, archiving, and transaction export processes across global corporate bank accounts, and conduct comprehensive monthly pricing audits and fee reviews to reconcile service charges and eliminate variances.

- Liquidity Transfers & Platform Expansion: Assist in corporate cash and liquidity management by executing recurring intercompany transfer setups, responding to external bank authorization requests, and configuring system variables to support the onboarding of new geographical markets or banking partners.

The Team You'll Work With

You’ll join the Treasury team, which plays a vital role in managing overall banking related activities and supporting corporate and customer money movement across Carta. As a Treasury Associate, you will act as a key partner to our internal business units, helping monitor, review, and reconcile payment transactions that flow through our banking networks every day.

In this role, you will collaborate cross-functionally with team members in Customer Support, Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and our global banking partners. Your day-to-day focus will center on resolving payment exceptions, administering critical banking portal access, and partnering on continuous process improvements to ensure a seamless, secure, and highly scalable money movement experience for our clients.

About You

We are looking for a detail-oriented, tech-forward, and highly responsible professional who meets the following criteria:

- Experienced in Banking & Treasury/Payment Operations: 3+ years of experience in a finance, accounting, or related role recommended, with 2+ years of dedicated experience specifically in Treasury operations, banking operations, or payment processing recommended.

- Technical Skillset & AI-Forward Mindset: Advanced user of core spreadsheet applications (Excel/Google Sheets) with baseline proficiency in data querying utilities (such as Looker or Metabase), and a strong passion for utilizing modern AI tools (such as Claude or Gemini) to automate manual tasks and drive process efficiencies.

- Expertise in Global Banking & Payment Systems: Proficient knowledge of banking services (ACH, wire, F/X transfers), reconciliations, payment rules, compliance and controls (such as NACHA guidelines, OFAC regulations, and bank portal administration).

- Autonomy & Project Ownership: A largely independent operator who is highly productive under general guidelines, exercises sound judgment to resolve moderate-scope operational issues using established procedures, and takes full ownership of low-complexity ad-hoc projects.

- Documentation & Detail Orientation: Rigorous attention to detail and an established record of executing tasks accurately and meeting tight deadlines, paired with a passion for creating and maintaining clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), reconciliations, and process flow mappings to eliminate single-source-of-knowledge risks.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication: A proactive collaborator who routinely partners within the treasury team and demonstrates emerging capabilities to work with Support, Product, Engineering, Legal, and Compliance, with the ability to clearly present analysis and communicate with business and technical stakeholders

At Carta, you’re not just an employee. You’re a builder who is creating  infrastructure that accelerates innovation and empowers more ownership. Cartans are helpful, relentless, unconventional and kind; representing Carta’s Identity Traits. They work collaboratively and cross functionally  to challenge the status quo; working towards a common goal of creating more owners in the private markets.

Salary

Carta’s compensation package includes a market competitive salary, equity for all full time roles, exceptional benefits, and, for applicable roles, commissions plans. Our minimum cash compensation range for this role is:
$93,500 - $120,000  in New York and San Francisco
$74,800 - $88,000  in Sandy, Utah

Final offers may vary from the amount listed based on geography, candidate experience and expertise, and other factors.

Disclosures:

- We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing a positive interview experience for every candidate. If accommodations due to a disability or medical condition are needed, please connect with the talent partner via email.

- Carta uses E-Verify in the United States for employment authorization. See the E-Verify and Department of Justice websites for more details.

- Please note that all official communications from us will come from an @carta.com or @carta-external.com domain. Report any contact from unapproved domains to security@carta.com.

Ideal candidates will be energized by building and managing impactful external relationships, driving cross-functional collaboration, digging into data, finding scalable and repeatable best practices, constructing strategic communications,  helping to change practices, and creating more owners across a rapidly evolving industry.

About You

You enjoy building lasting, productive relationships. You are curious and you’re driven to key in on relationships and strategies that benefit all sides. You dig in to find ways to work with others. You are data-informed. You are empathetic with respect to the needs of our ecosystem partners. You have a strong moral compass. You are motivated by making a material impact on our business. You are energized by sharing your learnings with others. You roll up your sleeves to partner with colleagues from across the company to explore what’s possible and drive results.

Qualifications

- An outgoing, natural networker with experience in building and maintaining relationships

- Knowledge of the VC Ecosystem in the UK, including legal firms, accelerators, VCs and the broader industry

- Familiarity with cap tables and venture-backed fundraising

- Strong communication, presentation, and networking skills, with experience attending industry events

Nice-to-Have

- Relevant network of contacts within the community, specifically encompassing Venture Capital firms and law firms firms, and the service providers that support them

- Prior experience building relationships or servicing funds as an industry partner supporting VC or private equity clients

- Prior experience managing relationships with high-profile ecosystem partners including investment funds, consultants, compliance providers, industry groups, investment platforms, wealth managers or other technology companies

- Understanding of fund formation, regulations that apply to funds, fund administration, fundraising, or valuation services.

The Problems You'll Solve

At Carta, we're transforming how private capital operates — connecting the software, services, and legal infrastructure that founders, fund managers, and legal teams depend on. We believe the problems we solve today unlock the opportunities of tomorrow. As a Demand Generation Manager for the Private Equity Business Unit, you'll work to:

- Research, develop, and execute end-to-end campaigns to drive net-new firms to our private equity and alternative assets products

- Collaborate with Sales, Product, and all parts of Marketing to test marketing strategies and drive quarterly business objectives through coordinated campaigns

- Own 6Sense ABM targeting, lifecycle streams, and SFDC campaign tracking for PE Investor prospects, using performance data to iterate and improve conversion at every stage

- Coordinate cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Success, BD, and Product to identify the highest-propensity accounts, surface key insights, and scale what's working into repeatable growth plays

- Help identify, drive, and execute on strategic growth initiatives and tests as we experiment and learn which levers are key growth opportunities for Carta

The Team You'll Work With

You'll be joining the Demand Generation team within the Revenue Marketing Org, reporting directly to the Senior Manager of Demand Generation.

The Demand Generation team is the tip of the spear for all growth and revenue driving aspects of Carta’s marketing organization. We own the full demand generation motion for all business units at Carta — from awareness campaigns and thought leadership to field events, outbound plays, and lifecycle nurtures. Our work is deeply cross-functional: we build campaigns in close partnership with Sales, PMM, Content, Events, and Finance, and we're accountable for a meaningful share of total pipeline every quarter. The team moves fast, experiments constantly, and brings both tactical execution and strategic thinking to every initiative.

About You

- Pipeline-obsessed. You've built and run multi-channel demand gen programs with a direct line to pipeline. You know how to connect campaign activity to opportunities, closed-won business, and marketing-sourced pipe, and you use that data to make better decisions.

- A campaign architect and operator in one. You're as comfortable writing an ABM strategy as you are managing the email build behind it, you bring both the strategic thinking and the hands-on execution to get programs into market.

- Cross-functional by default. You work naturally across Sales, Business Development, Operations and all aspects of the marketing org to align on messaging, coordinate timelines, and drive shared outcomes.

- Equal parts creative and analytical. You bring a marketer's instinct for what will resonate with a PE audience, a seller's understanding of what moves deals forward, and an operator's discipline for diving into the numbers to influence your marketing decisions.

- ABM-native. you understand how to build target account lists, structure intent-based plays, and sequence multi-channel campaigns. Experience with 6Sense is a strong plus.

- 6+ years of experience in demand gen recommended,  preferably in B2B SaaS, fintech, or financial services. Experience with 6Sense, Marketo, and Salesforce is a strong plus.

- Bonus if you have financial services or industry experience. You understand how private capital markets operate and you build campaigns that account for that reality.

jobs.description:
The Company You’ll Join

Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. For more information about our offices and culture, check out our Carta careers page .

The Team You'll Work With

You'll be joining our Inbound Compliance team.

This team sits at the front line of Carta's compliance function — managing the intake and resolution of KYC requests on behalf of some of the world's leading asset managers and private equity firms. You'll work in a high-volume, client-facing environment where accuracy, speed, and regulatory fluency aren't optional — they're the baseline.

The Problems You'll Solve

At Carta, our employees set out on a mission to unlock the power of equity ownership for more people in more places. We believe that the problems we solve today unlock the opportunities of tomorrow. As a KYC Analyst – Inbound Compliance, you'll work to:

- Own the KYC request lifecycle. Manage the intake, processing, and timely resolution of inbound KYC requests from clients and their counterparties, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks and every response meets the standard.

- Be the client's compliance guide. Serve as the primary point of contact for KYC inquiries, giving clients clear, confident answers on global KYC requirements so they can move their transactions forward.

- Uphold the regulatory bar. Review and validate KYC documentation for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with AML, KYC, and applicable international frameworks, and make the call when something doesn't pass muster.

- Keep records airtight. Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of all KYC requests and documentation in Carta's systems, so the team always has a clean audit trail.

- Stay ahead of a moving target. Monitor evolving KYC/AML regulations globally and apply updated requirements to daily work, ensuring Carta's compliance posture keeps pace with regulatory change.

About You

- Detail-oriented under pressure. You catch what others miss and you do it consistently, even when managing a high volume of concurrent requests against tight deadlines

- Confident and client-ready. You enjoy client  KYC conversations with senior stakeholders and counterparties, assertive, professional, and knowing when to escalate versus when to resolve.

- 1 to 2+ years of compliance experience. You have a working understanding of global KYC and AML frameworks and can apply them practically, not just cite them. AML/KYC certifications (ICA, ACAMS) are a plus but not required

- A proactive decision-maker. You don't wait to be told what to do. You assess the situation, apply the right framework, and move forward with minimal supervision

- Experienced in complex legal entities. Prior exposure to corporate banking, a legal service provider, or a fund compliance environment is a strong plus, particularly familiarity with offshore jurisdictions like Cayman or Luxembourg

- A communicator people trust. You write clearly, speak with confidence, and bring the same professionalism to client-facing correspondence as you do to internal work

- Able to manage a full plate. You handle multiple priorities simultaneously without dropping the ball, and you stay composed under tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment

- Building toward a compliance career. You have a genuine interest in AML/CFT compliance and legal services and you're looking for a place to grow, not just a job to fill

- Some legal or compliance exposure is a plus. Prior experience in a legal, compliance, or risk management environment is welcome but not required

Preferred but not required

- Experience with AI in practice. You've worked with AI tools or technology-driven workflows before and know how to apply them in real-world settings

- Prior experience in financial or legal services. A background at a law firm, legal services provider, fund administrator, or the compliance or legal department of a financial institution or asset manager will set you up well.

- Familiarity with KYC documentation. Experience reviewing or preparing KYC documentation packs, AML comfort letters, or UBO declarations is a meaningful advantage.

- Knowledge of private markets structures. Familiarity with fund formations, GP/LP relationships, and offshore holding structures including Luxembourg is a strong plus.

- Regulatory framework exposure. Any prior exposure to EU (including CSSF and AMLD requirements), UK (FCA), or US (FinCEN) AML/CFT frameworks will translate directly to this role.

- Qualifications. A degree in law, compliance, finance, or a related subject area, or a diploma in paralegal studies. Professional certifications such as ICA Certificate in AML or ACAMS are a plus but not required.

At Carta, you're not just an employee. You're a builder who is creating infrastructure that accelerates innovation and empowers more ownership. Cartans are helpful, relentless, unconventional and kind; representing Carta's Identity Traits. They work collaboratively and cross functionally to challenge the status quo; working towards a common goal of creating more owners in the private markets.
